title: Exact Certification and Guaranteed Termination for Two-Item Resource-Constrained Joint Replenishment
shortTitle: Exact certification for two-item joint replenishment
oneLine: For two periodically ordered items under nonnegative average-rate resource constraints, a resource-aware dual tail turns exact ratio enumeration into a guaranteed-termination certificate system and yields a new algebraic lower bound for the standard relaxation gap.
abstract: Joint replenishment saves a common ordering cost when periodic item schedules coincide, but those coincidences make the exact objective discontinuous in the period ratio. This unrefereed candidate resolves the stated two-item problem by reducing every coprime ratio to a one-dimensional exact scale optimization and retaining resource geometry in a Lagrange-dual tail certificate. A strict synchronisation argument proves that unrestricted ratio enumeration terminates after finitely many ratios whenever the common setup cost is positive; no polynomial runtime is claimed. For the standard convex relaxation, a real-coefficient cap-reduction lemma reduces worst-case gap analysis to itemwise frequency caps. A certified triple-tie family has a unique algebraic family maximum gamma approximately 1.11188959394, improving the packaged lower bound while leaving the exact global gap open. Four finite witnesses, two interval-family verifiers, negative controls, 16 tests, deterministic documents, and producer-side fresh-extraction replay pass. There is no independent reproduction, formal verification, specialist review, peer review, field validation, complete priority audit, or evidence of operational savings.
narration: Joint replenishment asks when two items should be ordered so that they can share a common fixed cost. The difficulty is arithmetic: periodic schedules share an order only when their cycle lengths align, so a tiny change in the ratio can change the pattern of coincidences. This candidate gives an exact certificate system for the two-item model with nonnegative average-rate resource constraints. For each rational cycle ratio, the problem becomes a one-dimensional convex scale calculation. The key new ingredient is a resource-aware tail bound. A Lagrange dual preserves the capacity geometry that an older unconstrained bound discarded, and every unexamined ratio receives a certified lower bound. The paper also proves that synchronisation always creates a strict advantage over the best desynchronised policy when the common setup cost is positive. Consequently, unrestricted ratio enumeration eventually closes, although no polynomial runtime is claimed. A second contribution concerns the standard convex relaxation used to lower-bound the problem. The candidate proves that, over real resource coefficients, worst-case gap analysis can be reduced to separate frequency caps. Inside a canonical triple-tie family it then certifies a unique algebraic maximum of about 1.11188959394. This is a rigorous global lower bound, not the exact global gap. The package contains exact witnesses, interval and elimination certificates, solver-independent checkers, negative controls, 16 tests, deterministic papers, and a fresh-extraction replay receipt. All of those checks were performed within the producing workflow. The result remains an unrefereed candidate with no independent reproduction, formal proof-assistant verification, specialist review, peer review, field validation, complete novelty audit, or demonstrated operating savings.

problem.name: Two-item resource-constrained continuous-time joint replenishment and the gap of relaxation (P)

keyResults: For every fixed coprime period ratio, the resource-constrained two-item objective reduces to an exact one-dimensional convex scale problem with a rational or quadratic-radical optimum.
A nonnegative Lagrange-dual certificate for the constrained desynchronised optimum yields a resource-aware lower bound for every omitted ratio.

When the common ordering cost is positive, a rational synchronised policy lies strictly below the desynchronised optimum, so unbounded ratio enumeration is guaranteed to terminate after finitely many ratios; no polynomial runtime is claimed.
Over nonnegative real resource systems, the supremum gap of relaxation (P) is unchanged when analysis is restricted to item-specific frequency caps; no rational-data continuity identity is claimed.

A canonical triple-tie cap family has a unique algebraic family maximum gamma satisfying 262 gamma^4 - 916 gamma^3 + 863 gamma^2 + 150 gamma - 375 = 0, with gamma approximately 1.11188959394, establishing a global lower bound but not the exact global gap.
A finite two-item alignment-configuration hull closes all four bundled regression certificates, but no multi-item separation or rounding theorem is supplied.
evidence: An 8-page candidate theorem paper and 3-page practitioner brief in PDF and TeX; exact Python solver and fail-closed CLI; four finite rational/radical witnesses; resource-dual and tail certificates; interval verifiers for the original and canonical families; exact quartic isolation and elimination checks; a finite alignment-configuration regression certificate; schema and semantic-mutation controls; 16 tests under ordinary and optimized Python; deterministic figures and PDFs; an 82-entry SHA-256 manifest; a producer adversarial review; and producer-side fresh-extraction replay of the immutable ZIP. These checks do not constitute independent reproduction or external theorem verification.
statusDetail: Unrefereed candidate computer-assisted result. Producer-side solver-independent replay, fresh-extraction regeneration, mutation controls, fail-closed output checks, deterministic document builds, GitHub/Zenodo archive matching, and public file readback pass. The analytic manuscript and supplied certificates have not been independently reconstructed by an unaffiliated party or formalized in a proof assistant. There has been no external specialist audit, editorial peer review, field validation, complete novelty or priority audit, or demonstration that a certified nominal policy yields operational savings. The exact global relaxation gap, multi-item alignment relaxation and rounding, column-sparsity frontier, three-item oracle, robust uncertainty, calendar phases, pointwise capacity, and wider theory remain open.

openProblems: Determine the exact two-item and global integrality gaps, or obtain substantially tighter upper certificates that are proved to match the same relaxation and model.
Construct a multi-item alignment-aware relaxation with polynomial separation and a rounding theorem while preserving the exact two-item regression suite.
Classify the column-sparsity k=1, k=2, and fixed-k approximation or hardness frontier.
Build and independently reproduce a complete exact three-item oracle, including its regime and tail proof objects.
Develop robust correlated-uncertainty regions rather than one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis.
Extend the model to calendar phases, fixed delivery dates, and pointwise capacity without erasing synchronisation semantics.
Run a preregistered field pilot with reconciled marginal costs, operational feasibility gates, guardrails, and stop rules.
Obtain independent mathematical reconstruction, specialist review, proof-assistant formalization, and a broader novelty and priority audit.
